title.zh: 卷一百三十一 列傳第八十一: 李勉 李皋 子像古 道古
title.en: Volume 131 Biographies 81: Li Mian, Li Gao, Zi Xianggu, Dao Gu
title.raw: 卷一百三十一 列傳第八十一: 李勉 李皋 子像古 道古 Volume 131 Biographies 81: Li Mian, Li Gao, Zi Xianggu, Dao Gu

sentences.zh: 李勉，字玄卿，鄭王元懿曾孫也。

translations.literal: Li Mian, styled Xuanqing, was a great-grandson of Prince Yuanyi of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mian, whose courtesy name was Xuanqing, was a great-grandson of Prince Yuanyi of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 父擇言，為漢褒相岐四州刺史、安德郡公，所歷皆以嚴干聞。

translations.literal: His father Zeyan served as prefect of the four prefectures of Han, Bao, Xiang, and Qi and as Duke of Ande Commandery; in every post he was known for stern integrity.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Zeyan held the posts of prefect of Han, Bao, Xiang, and Qi and Duke of Ande Commandery, and wherever he served he won a reputation for strict, capable administration.

sentences.zh: 在漢州，張嘉貞為益州長史、判都督事，性簡貴，待管內刺史禮隔，而引擇言同榻，坐談政理，時人榮之。

translations.literal: While in Hanzhou, Zhang Jiazhen was acting prefect of Yizhou and concurrently judged the military commission; of a reserved and lofty nature, he kept distant ceremonial distance from the prefects under his jurisdiction, yet he had Zeyan share his couch and sit discussing statecraft—men of the time counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeyan was in Han Prefecture, Zhang Jiazhen was acting prefect of Yizhou and concurrently judged regional military affairs. Though reserved and lofty in manner, Zhang kept the prefects in his circuit at a formal distance, yet he had Zeyan sit with him on the same couch to discuss government; contemporaries regarded this as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 勉幼勤經史，長而沉雅清峻，宗於虛玄，以近屬陪位，累授開封尉。

translations.literal: Mian in youth applied himself to the classics and histories; grown up he was grave, refined, and clear in bearing, devoted to Daoist subtlety, and by virtue of kinship to the throne he repeatedly received appointment as aide in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Mian studied the classics and histories diligently; in maturity he was grave, elegant, and austere in manner, inclined toward Daoist learning, and because of his proximity to the imperial clan he was repeatedly appointed aide in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時升平日久，且汴州水陸所湊，邑居龐雜，號為難理，勉與聯尉盧成軌等，並有擒奸擿伏之名。

translations.literal: The age was long at peace, and moreover Bianzhou, where land and water routes converged, had crowded, tangled settlements and was known as hard to govern; Mian together with fellow aides such as Lu Chenggui all won fame for seizing wrongdoers and exposing hidden crime.
translations.idiomatic: Peace had lasted many years, and Bianzhou—where waterways and highways met—was densely settled and notoriously difficult to administer. Mian, together with fellow aides such as Lu Chenggui, earned a name for capturing criminals and exposing concealed wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 至德初，從至靈武，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhide era he followed the court to Lingwu and was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Zhide period he accompanied the court to Lingwu and was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 屬朝廷右武，勳臣恃寵，多不知禮。

translations.literal: It happened that the court favored military men; meritorious ministers, relying on favor, for the most part did not observe ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court leaned toward military power, and meritorious ministers, trusting in imperial favor, often showed little regard for ceremony.

sentences.zh: 大將管崇嗣於行在朝堂背闕而坐，言笑自若，勉劾之，拘於有司，肅宗特原之，歎曰：「吾有李勉，始知朝廷尊也。

translations.literal: The great general Guan Congsi sat in the mobile court hall with his back to the imperial audience hall, talking and laughing as he pleased; Mian impeached him and had him detained by the appropriate offices. Emperor Suzong specially pardoned him and sighed, "Only now that I have Li Mian do I know that the court is to be honored."
translations.idiomatic: The general Guan Congsi sat in the temporary palace hall with his back to the throne, chatting and laughing at ease. Mian impeached him and had him held by the proper authorities. Emperor Suzong personally pardoned him, yet sighed and said, "Only now that I have Li Mian do I understand what it means to honor the court."

sentences.zh: 」遷司膳員外郎。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to vice director in the Office of Palace Provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to vice director in the Office of Palace Provisions.

sentences.zh: 時關東獻俘百餘，詔並處斬，囚有仰天歎者，勉過問之，對曰：「某被脅制守官，非逆者。

translations.literal: At that time more than a hundred captives from east of the Pass were presented; an edict ordered them all executed. One prisoner sighed toward heaven; Mian passed by and questioned him, and he replied, "I was compelled to hold office and was not a rebel."
translations.idiomatic: At that time more than a hundred captives from east of the Pass were presented to the court, and an edict ordered them all put to death. One prisoner looked up to heaven and sighed; Mian questioned him, and he answered, "I was forced to hold my post—I was no rebel."

sentences.zh: 」勉乃哀之，上言曰：「元惡未殄，遭點污者半天下，皆欲澡心歸化。

translations.literal: " Mian then took pity on him and memorialized, saying, "The chief villain is not yet destroyed; those who were stained number half the empire, and all wish to cleanse their hearts and return to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: " Mian was moved to pity and submitted a memorial: "The chief rebels are not yet destroyed. Half the empire has been tainted by association, yet all wish to cleanse their hearts and submit again.

sentences.zh: 若盡殺之，是驅天下以資兇逆也。

translations.literal: If they are all killed, this is driving the empire to supply the vicious rebels."
translations.idiomatic: If we execute them all, we will drive the whole empire into the rebels' camp."

sentences.zh: 」肅宗遽令奔騎宥釋，由是歸化日至。

translations.literal: " Emperor Suzong immediately sent mounted couriers to pardon and release them; from this day submissions increased daily.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong at once sent mounted couriers to pardon and release them, and from that day defections and submissions grew daily.

sentences.zh: 克復西京，累歷清要，四遷至河南少尹。

translations.literal: When the Western Capital was recovered, he successively held pure and important posts and was promoted four times to vice governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After the recovery of the Western Capital he rose through a series of prestigious offices and was promoted four times to vice governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 累為河東節度王思禮、朔方河東都統李國貞行軍司馬，尋遷梁州都督、山南西道觀察使。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served as campaigning staff officer to Hedong military commissioner Wang Sil and to Li Guozhen, supreme commander of Shuofang and Hedong; soon he was transferred to regional inspector of Liangzhou and observation commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as campaigning staff officer to Hedong commissioner Wang Sil and to Li Guozhen, supreme commander of Shuofang and Hedong, and was soon appointed regional inspector of Liangzhou and observation commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 勉以故吏前密縣尉王晬勤干，俾攝南鄭令，俄有詔處死，勉問其故，乃為權幸所誣。

translations.literal: Mian, because his former subordinate Wang Hui, former magistrate of Mi County, was diligent and capable, had him act as magistrate of Nanzheng; shortly an edict ordered his execution. Mian asked the reason and learned he had been slandered by the powerful and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Mian had his former subordinate Wang Hui, once magistrate of Mi County and a man of proven diligence, act as magistrate of Nanzheng. Soon an edict arrived ordering Wang's execution. When Mian inquired, he found that favorites at court had framed him.

sentences.zh: 勉詢將吏曰：「上方藉牧宰為人父母，豈以譖言而殺不辜乎！

translations.literal: Mian questioned his officers and clerks, saying, "His Majesty relies on prefects and magistrates as fathers and mothers to the people—how could he kill the innocent on a slanderer's word!"
translations.idiomatic: Mian asked his officers and clerks, "The throne depends on local officials to be fathers and mothers to the people. How could it put an innocent man to death on a whispered accusation?"

sentences.zh: 」即停詔拘晬，飛表上聞，晬遂獲宥，而勉竟為執政所非，追入為大理少卿。

translations.literal: " He at once halted the edict and detained Hui, sent a flying memorial to inform the throne, and Hui thereby obtained pardon; yet Mian in the end was faulted by those in power and was recalled to serve as vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately withheld the edict and detained Wang, then sent an urgent memorial to the throne. Wang was spared, but Mian was criticized by those in power and recalled to serve as vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 謁見，面陳王晬無罪，政事條舉，盡力吏也。

translations.literal: On audience he stated to the emperor's face that Wang Hui was guiltless, that his administration was orderly in every item, and that he was an official who gave his full strength.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he told the emperor face to face that Wang Hui was innocent, that his administration was thorough and well ordered, and that he was an official who gave his full effort.

sentences.zh: 肅宗嘉其守正，乃除太常少卿。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong praised his uprightness and thereupon appointed him vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong praised his integrity and appointed him vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 王晬後以推擇拜大理評事、龍門令，終有能名，時稱知人。

translations.literal: Wang Hui later, on recommendation, was appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Longmen; he ended with a reputation for ability, and men of the time said Mian knew how to judge men.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui was later recommended and appointed reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and magistrate of Longmen. He ended his career with a reputation for ability, and contemporaries said Mian had a gift for recognizing talent.

sentences.zh: 肅宗將大用勉，會李輔國寵任，意欲勉降禮於己。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong was about to employ Mian in great matters when Li Fuguo, in favor and trust, wished Mian to lower ritual deference toward himself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was on the point of giving Mian major responsibilities when Li Fuguo, then in favor, expected Mian to defer to him in ritual precedence.

sentences.zh: 勉不為之屈，竟為所抑，出歷汾州、虢州刺史，改京兆尹、檢校右庶子、兼御史中丞、都畿觀察使。

translations.literal: Mian would not yield to him and in the end was suppressed by him; he went out and successively served as prefect of Fenzhou and Guozhou, then was changed to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, acting right vice heir apparent, and concurrently censor in chief and observation commissioner of the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: Mian refused to yield and was eventually blocked by him. He was sent out to serve successively as prefect of Fen and Guo, then appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, acting right vice heir apparent, censor in chief, and observation commissioner of the Capital Region.

sentences.zh: 尋兼河南尹，明年罷尹，以中丞歸西台，又除江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally Henan metropolitan governor; the next year he left the governorship, returned to the western bureau as censor in chief, and was again appointed observation commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He soon also held the Henan metropolitan governorship. The following year he left that post, returned to the Censorate as chief censor, and was appointed observation commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 賊帥陳莊連陷江西州縣，偏將呂太一、武日升相繼背叛，勉與諸道力戰，悉攻平之。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Chen Zhuang successively captured prefectures and counties of Jiangxi; subordinate generals Lü Taiyi and Wu Risheng in turn rebelled; Mian with the forces of various circuits fought strenuously and attacked until all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Chen Zhuang seized one Jiangxi prefecture and county after another, while subordinate generals Lü Taiyi and Wu Risheng rebelled in turn. Mian fought alongside troops from other circuits until every uprising was suppressed.

sentences.zh: 部人有父病，以蠱道為木偶人，署勉名位，瘞於其隴，或以告，曰：「為父禳災，亦可矜也。

translations.literal: A man of his command had a father ill; by sorcery he made a wooden puppet, inscribed Mian's name and rank, and buried it on his mound. Someone reported it, and Mian said, "It was to avert disaster for his father—this too may be pitied."
translations.idiomatic: A subordinate whose father was ill used sorcery to fashion a wooden effigy bearing Mian's name and title and buried it on the family grave mound. When someone reported it, Mian said, "He was trying to ward off disaster for his father—that is pitiable enough."

sentences.zh: 」捨之。

translations.literal: " He released him.
translations.idiomatic: He let the matter go.

sentences.zh: 大歷二年，來朝，拜京兆尹、兼御史大夫，政尚簡肅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dali he came to court and was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and concurrently grand censor; his administration favored simplicity and severity.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Dali era he came to court and was appointed metropolitan governor of Jingzhao and concurrently grand censor. His rule was marked by simplicity and strictness.

sentences.zh: 宦官魚朝恩為觀軍容使，仍知國子監事，恃寵含威，天憲在舌。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yu Chao'en was army-observing commissioner and still supervised the Directorate of the Imperial Academy; relying on favor he harbored awe, and heaven's law lay on his tongue.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yu Chao'en was army-observing commissioner and still supervised the Imperial Academy. Trusting in favor, he carried menace in his bearing, and the law itself seemed to rest on his tongue.

sentences.zh: 前尹黎干寫心候事，動必求媚，每朝恩入監，傾府人吏具數百人之餼以待之。

translations.literal: The previous governor Li Gan laid bare his heart in waiting on affairs and in every move sought to flatter; whenever Chao'en entered the directorate, he emptied the prefecture's clerks and attendants to prepare provisions for several hundred men to await him.
translations.idiomatic: The previous governor, Li Gan, fawned on him in every matter. Whenever Chao'en visited the Academy, Li Gan mobilized the entire prefectural staff to prepare food for hundreds of men in advance of his arrival.

sentences.zh: 及勉蒞職旬月，朝恩入監，府吏先期有請，勉曰：「軍容使判國子監事，勉候太學，軍容宜厚具主禮。

translations.literal: When Mian had been in office about ten days, Chao'en entered the directorate; prefectural clerks asked in advance, and Mian said, "The army-observing commissioner concurrently judges the Imperial Academy; Mian awaits him at the Imperial University—the commissioner ought richly to furnish the host's rites.
translations.idiomatic: About ten days after Mian took office, Chao'en visited the Academy. The prefectural staff asked in advance how to receive him. Mian said, "As army-observing commissioner he also supervises the Academy. I shall receive him at the Imperial University; the commissioner should provide the full hospitality due a host there.

sentences.zh: 勉忝京尹，軍容倘惠顧府廷，豈敢不具蔬饌。

translations.literal: Mian is unworthy as metropolitan governor; if the commissioner should favor the prefectural court with a visit, how would I dare not furnish a simple meal."
translations.idiomatic: As metropolitan governor I would be unworthy if he did not visit; but should he honor the prefectural offices with a call, I would of course provide a modest meal."

sentences.zh: 」朝恩聞而銜之，因不復至太學，勉亦尋受代。

translations.literal: Chao'en heard and harbored resentment; he therefore did not again go to the Imperial University, and Mian soon accepted replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Chao'en heard this and bore a grudge. He never visited the University again, and Mian was soon replaced.

sentences.zh: 四年，除廣州刺史，兼嶺南節度觀察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was dismissed as prefect of Guangzhou and concurrently Lingnan military commissioner and observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed prefect of Guangzhou and concurrently military commissioner and observation commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 番禺賊帥馮崇道、桂州叛將硃濟時等阻洞為亂，前後累歲，陷沒十餘州。

translations.literal: The Panyu bandit chief Feng Chongdao, the Guizhou rebel general Zhu Jishi, and others blocked the mountain passes and made disorder; for years before and after, more than ten prefectures were lost.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit leader Feng Chongdao of Panyu, the Guizhou rebel Zhu Jishi, and others had used the mountain passes to raise rebellion for years, seizing more than ten prefectures.

sentences.zh: 勉至，遣將李觀與容州刺史王翃人並力招討，悉斬之，五嶺平。

translations.literal: When Mian arrived, he sent the general Li Guan and Rongzhou prefect Wang Hongren to join forces in summons and suppression; all were beheaded and the Five Ridges were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian arrived he sent the general Li Guan and Rongzhou prefect Wang Hongren to campaign together against them. All the rebel leaders were executed and the Five Ridges were pacified.

sentences.zh: 前後西域舶泛海至者歲才四五，勉性廉潔，舶來都不檢閱，故末年至者四十餘。

translations.literal: Before and after, Western Region ships crossing the sea arrived only four or five a year; Mian by nature was incorrupt, and when ships came he did not inspect them at all, so that in his last year more than forty arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier years only four or five Western merchant ships reached port each year. Mian was by nature incorruptible and never inspected incoming vessels, so that in his final year more than forty ships called.

sentences.zh: 在官累年，器用車服無增飾。

translations.literal: During many years in office, his vessels, implements, carriages, and dress had no added ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his years in office his household goods, carriages, and dress showed no added luxury.

sentences.zh: 及代歸，至石門停舟，悉搜家人所貯南貨犀象諸物，投之江中，耆老以為可繼前朝宋璟、盧奐、李朝隱之徒。

translations.literal: When he was replaced and returned, at Shimen he moored his boat, searched out all southern goods, rhinoceros horn, ivory, and such things stored by his household, and cast them into the river; elders thought he could follow the men of the previous dynasty—Song Jing, Lu Huan, Li Chaoyin, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office and returned north, he moored at Shimen, gathered every piece of southern tribute goods, rhinoceros horn, ivory, and the like that his household had stored, and threw them into the river. Local elders said he could stand beside such earlier models of integrity as Song Jing, Lu Huan, and Li Chaoyin.

sentences.zh: 人吏詣闕請立碑，代宗許之。

translations.literal: Officials and clerks went to the palace to request that a stele be erected; Emperor Daizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials petitioned the throne to erect a memorial stele, and Emperor Daizong approved.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 及滑亳永平軍節度令狐彰卒，遺表舉勉自代，因除之。

translations.literal: When Linghu Zhang, military commissioner of the Huabo-Yongping army, died, his final memorial recommended Mian to replace him, and Mian was thereupon appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Linghu Zhang, military commissioner of the Huabo-Yongping army, died, his final memorial recommended Mian as his successor, and Mian was appointed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 在鎮八年，以舊德清重，不嚴而理，東諸侯雖暴驁者，亦宗敬之。

translations.literal: During eight years in the command, by his old virtue he was pure and weighty; without severity there was order, and even the eastern feudatories who were violent and proud honored and revered him.
translations.idiomatic: He held the command for eight years. His long-standing moral authority was so weighty that order prevailed without harshness, and even the most unruly eastern governors treated him with respect.

sentences.zh: 十一年，汴宋留後田神玉卒，詔加勉汴州刺史、汴宋節度使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Tian Shenyu, acting commander of Bian-Song, died; an edict added to Mian the posts of Bianzhou prefect and Bian-Song military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Tian Shenyu, acting commander of Bian-Song, died. An edict appointed Mian prefect of Bianzhou and military commissioner of Bian-Song.

sentences.zh: 未行，汴州將李靈曜阻兵，北結田承嗣，承嗣使侄悅將銳兵戍之。

translations.literal: Before he set out, the Bianzhou general Li Lingyao obstructed the army; north he joined Tian Chengsi, and Chengsi sent his nephew Yue to lead crack troops to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the post, the Bianzhou general Li Lingyao rebelled and allied himself with Tian Chengsi to the north. Chengsi sent his nephew Tian Yue with elite troops to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 詔勉與李忠臣、馬燧等攻討，大破之，悅僅以身免。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Mian together with Li Zhongchen, Ma Sui, and others to attack and suppress; they inflicted a great defeat, and Yue barely escaped with his person.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Mian, Li Zhongchen, Ma Sui, and others to attack. They won a crushing victory; Tian Yue escaped only with his life.

sentences.zh: 靈曜北走，勉騎將杜如江擒之以獻，代宗褒賞甚厚。

translations.literal: Lingyao fled north; Mian's cavalry general Du Rujiang captured him and presented him; Emperor Daizong rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Lingyao fled north, but Mian's cavalry officer Du Rujiang captured him and presented him to the throne. Emperor Daizong rewarded Mian lavishly.

sentences.zh: 既而李忠臣代鎮汴州，而勉仍舊鎮。

translations.literal: Shortly Li Zhongchen replaced him in garrisoning Bianzhou, while Mian remained in his former command.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen was then assigned to garrison Bianzhou while Mian retained his original command.

sentences.zh: 忠臣遇下貪虐，明年為麾下所逐，詔復加勉汴宋節度使，移理汴州，餘並如故。

translations.literal: Zhongchen in dealing with subordinates was greedy and cruel; the next year he was driven out by his own troops. An edict again added to Mian the Bian-Song military commissionership; he moved administration to Bianzhou, the rest remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongchen treated his men with greed and cruelty, and the following year his own troops drove him out. An edict restored the Bian-Song commissionership to Mian and moved his headquarters to Bianzhou; his other titles remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，加檢校吏部尚書，尋加平章事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong succeeded, Mian was given acting minister of civil office; soon he was made associate chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong succeeded to the throne, Mian was made acting minister of civil appointments and soon appointed associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，檢校左僕射，充河南汴宋滑亳河陽等道都統，餘如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong he was made acting left vice director of the Secretariat and supreme commander of the Henan, Bian-Song, Hua-Bo, Yongping, and Heyang circuits, the rest as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong he was made acting left vice director of the Secretariat and supreme commander of the Henan, Bian-Song, Hua-Bo, Yongping, and Heyang circuits, with his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 四年，李希烈反，以他盜為名，悉眾來寇汴州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Li Xilie rebelled; under the name of other bandits he brought his entire force to attack Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Li Xilie rebelled. Rallying under the banner of other bandit groups, he led his full army against Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 勉城守累月，救援莫至，謂其將曰：「希烈兇逆殘酷，若與較力，必多殺無辜，吾不忍也。

translations.literal: Mian defended the city for many months; relief did not arrive. He said to his generals, "Xilie is vicious, rebellious, and cruel; if we match strength with him, many innocents will surely be killed—I cannot bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Mian held the city for months, but no relief force came. He told his generals, "Xilie is savage and cruel. If we fight him head on, countless innocents will die. I cannot bring myself to do that."

sentences.zh: 」遂潛師潰圍，南奔宋州。

translations.literal: He thereupon secretly led his troops in breaking the encirclement and fled south to Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly led his troops out through the siege lines and fled south to Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔以司徒平章事征。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him as minister of education and associate chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him to court as minister of education and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 既至朝廷，素服請罪，優詔復其位，勉引過備位而已。

translations.literal: When he reached the court he wore plain dress and asked punishment; a gracious edict restored his position, and Mian only acknowledged fault and filled his post.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he appeared in plain dress to accept blame. A gracious edict restored his rank, and Mian simply acknowledged his fault and resumed his duties.

sentences.zh: 無何，盧杞自新州員外司馬除澧州刺史，給事中袁高以杞邪佞蠹政，貶未塞責，停詔執表，遂授澧州別駕。

translations.literal: Before long Lu Qi was dismissed from acting prefect of Xinzhou to prefect of Lizhou; the attendant Yuan Gao, because Qi was wicked, fawning, and a plague on government, held that demotion did not answer the crime, stopped the edict and submitted a memorial, and Qi was thereupon made Lizhou assistant prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Lu Qi was transferred from acting prefect of Xinzhou to prefect of Lizhou. The attendant Yuan Gao argued that Qi was wicked and corrupt and that demotion was insufficient punishment. He blocked the edict and submitted a memorial, and Qi was reduced to assistant prefect of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 他日，上謂勉曰：「眾人皆言盧杞奸邪，朕何不知！

translations.literal: Another day the emperor said to Mian, "Everyone says Lu Qi is treacherous and wicked—how would I not know!"
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion the emperor said to Mian, "Everyone says Lu Qi is treacherous and wicked. Do you think I do not know that?"

sentences.zh: 卿知其狀乎？

translations.literal: Do you know his condition?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you know what he is really like?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「天下皆知其奸邪，獨陛下不知，所以為奸邪也。

translations.literal: He replied, "All the empire knows he is treacherous and wicked; only Your Majesty does not know—this is why he is treacherous and wicked."
translations.idiomatic: Mian answered, "The whole empire knows he is treacherous and wicked. Only Your Majesty does not know it. That is precisely what makes him treacherous and wicked."

sentences.zh: 」時人多其正直，然自是見疏。

translations.literal: Men of the time mostly praised his uprightness, yet from this he was seen at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries admired his blunt honesty, but from that point he fell out of favor.

sentences.zh: 累表辭位，遂罷知政事，加太了太保。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized to resign his post and was thereupon removed from participation in government affairs and made crown prince grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to resign and was relieved of his duties as chief minister, receiving instead the post of grand mentor of the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 貞元四年卒，年七十二，上頗愍悼之，冊贈太傅，賻物有差，喪葬官給。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyuan he died, age seventy-two; the emperor was quite moved to pity and mourning, posthumously enfeoffed him as grand tutor, gave funeral goods in graded measure, and supplied officials for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhenyuan at the age of seventy-two. The emperor was deeply grieved and posthumously enfeoffed him as grand tutor, granted funeral goods in due measure, and provided official support for the burial.

sentences.zh: 勉坦率素淡，好古尚奇，清廉簡易，為宗臣之表。

translations.literal: Mian was frank and plain by nature, fond of antiquity and prizing the unusual, pure, incorrupt, simple and easy in manner—a model among imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was frank and unpretentious by nature, loved antiquity and prized the unusual, and lived with incorruptible simplicity. He was regarded as a model among the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 善鼓琴，好屬詩，妙知音律，能自制琴，又有巧思。

translations.literal: He was skilled at playing the zither, fond of composing verse, subtle in knowing pitch and regulation, able to make zithers himself, and again had ingenious thought.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at the zither, enjoyed composing poetry, had a fine ear for music, could build his own instruments, and possessed a ready ingenuity in other arts as well.

sentences.zh: ，及在相位向二十年，祿俸皆遺親黨，身沒而無私積。

translations.literal: Moreover, while in the chancellorship for nearly twenty years, his salary and stipends were all given to kin and associates; when his person perished there was no private accumulation.
translations.idiomatic: During nearly twenty years as chief minister he gave away his salary and stipends to relatives and friends, and when he died he left no private wealth.

sentences.zh: 其在大官，禮賢下士，終始盡心。

translations.literal: When he was a high minister, he honored the worthy and lowered himself toward scholars, from beginning to end giving his full heart.
translations.idiomatic: As a high minister he honored talent and treated scholars with respect, devoting himself wholeheartedly from first to last.

sentences.zh: 以名士李巡、張參為判官，卒於幕，三歲之內，每遇宴飲，必設虛位於筵次，陳膳執酹，辭色心妻惻，論者美之。

translations.literal: He took the noted scholars Li Xun and Zhang Can as administrative aides; they died in his staff. Within three years, whenever he met with feasting and drinking, he always set an empty seat at the place in the banquet, set out food and held libation, his words and expression heartsick and sorrowful—discussants praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed the renowned scholars Li Xun and Zhang Can as his administrative aides; both died while serving on his staff. For three years thereafter, whenever he held a banquet he set out an empty place at the table, offered food and poured libations, his words and bearing full of grief. Commentators praised his devotion.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「勉失守梁城，亦可貶也。

translations.literal: Some said, "Mian lost Liang city and might also be demoted."
translations.idiomatic: Some said that Mian deserved demotion for losing Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 」 議者曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Discussants said, "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Others replied, "That is not so."

sentences.zh: 當賊烈之始亂，其慓悍陰禍，兇焰不可當，天方厚其毒而降之罰。

translations.literal: When the rebel Xilie first made disorder, his fierceness and hidden harm, his vicious flame could not be withstood; heaven was just then heaping his poison and sending down punishment upon him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xilie first rebelled, his ferocity and hidden malice made his onslaught irresistible. Heaven itself was heaping up his wickedness before bringing down punishment upon him.

sentences.zh: 況勉應變非長，援軍莫至，又其時關輔已俶擾矣，人心已動搖矣。

translations.literal: Moreover Mian was not long skilled in meeting change; relief armies did not arrive; and at that time the Guanzhong region was already stirring in disorder, and men's hearts were already shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Mian was not skilled in military emergencies, no relief force arrived, and by then the capital region was already in turmoil and public morale was collapsing.

sentences.zh: 以文吏之才，當虎狼之隊，其全師奔宋，非量力之恥也。

translations.literal: With the talent of a civil clerk to face a pack of tigers and wolves—his preserving the army intact and fleeing to Song was not the shame of misjudging one's strength.
translations.idiomatic: A civil official facing a wolfish army—his withdrawal with the army intact to Songzhou was no disgrace of overreaching his capacity.

sentences.zh: 與其坐受喪敗，不猶愈乎！」

translations.literal: Compared with sitting and receiving defeat and ruin, was it not rather better!"
translations.idiomatic: Surely that was better than staying to suffer total defeat!"

sentences.zh: 李皋，字子蘭，曹王明玄孫，嗣王戢之子。

translations.literal: Li Gao, styled Zilan, was a great-great-grandson of Prince Mingxuan of Cao and son of the heir prince Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gao, whose courtesy name was Zilan, was a great-great-grandson of Prince Mingxuan of Cao and son of the heir prince Ji.

sentences.zh: 少補左司御率府兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: In youth he was appointed military staff officer in the Left Bureau of the Heir Apparent's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was appointed military staff officer in the Left Bureau of the Heir Apparent's Guard.

sentences.zh: 天寶十一載嗣封授都水使者，三遷至秘書少監，皆同正。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianbao, on succeeding to the enfeoffment he was given the post of commissioner of waterways; three promotions brought him to vice director of the Secretariat, all as acting.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tianbao, upon inheriting his princely title, he was appointed commissioner of waterways. Three promotions brought him to vice director of the Secretariat, each time in an acting capacity.

sentences.zh: 多智數，善因事以自便。

translations.literal: He had many stratagems and was skilled at turning affairs to his own convenience.
translations.idiomatic: He was resourceful and adept at turning circumstances to his advantage.

sentences.zh: 奉太妃鄭氏以孝聞。

translations.literal: In serving the consort dowager Lady Zheng he was known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: He was renowned for the filial devotion with which he cared for his mother, Consort Dowager Lady Zheng.

sentences.zh: 上元初，京師旱，米斗直數千，死者甚多。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan the capital suffered drought; rice was several thousand per dou and very many died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era the capital suffered drought. Grain cost thousands of cash per dou, and many people starved to death.

sentences.zh: 皋度俸不足養，亟請外官，不允，乃故抵微法，貶溫州長史。

translations.literal: Gao judged his stipend insufficient to support his household and urgently requested an outside post; it was not granted, so he deliberately touched a minor law and was demoted to acting prefect of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao found his salary insufficient to support his household and repeatedly asked for an outside appointment. When this was refused, he deliberately committed a minor infraction and was demoted to acting prefect of Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 無幾，攝行州事。

translations.literal: Before long he was entrusted to administer prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was entrusted with the administration of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲儉，州有官粟數十萬斛，皋欲行賑救，掾吏叩頭乞候上旨，皋曰：「夫人日不再食，當死，安暇稟命！

translations.literal: The year was lean; the prefecture had several hundred thousand hu of official grain. Gao wished to carry out relief; clerks knocked their heads begging to await imperial command. Gao said, "When people cannot eat twice a day they must die—where is leisure to report for orders!"
translations.idiomatic: That year harvests failed, yet the prefecture held several hundred thousand hu of government grain. Gao wished to distribute relief, but his clerks begged on their knees to await imperial approval. Gao said, "When people cannot eat twice a day they die. Who has time to wait for orders from the capital?"

sentences.zh: 若殺我一身，活數千人命，利莫大焉。

translations.literal: If killing my one person gives life to several thousand persons, the benefit could not be greater."
translations.idiomatic: If my death saves thousands of lives, the gain could hardly be greater."

sentences.zh: 」於是開倉盡散之，以擅貸之罪，飛章自劾。

translations.literal: He thereupon opened the granaries and dispersed all of it; on the charge of unauthorized lending he sent a flying memorial impeaching himself.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the granaries and distributed the grain. Then he sent an urgent memorial impeaching himself for unauthorized lending of government stores.

sentences.zh: 天子聞而嘉之，答以優詔，就加少府監。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven heard and praised it, answered with a gracious edict, and on the spot added the post of vice director of the Palace Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and praised him, replying with a gracious edict and promoting him on the spot to vice director of the Palace Workshops.

sentences.zh: 皋行縣，見一媼垂白而泣，哀而問之，對曰：「李氏之婦，有二子：鈞、鍔，宦游二十年不歸，貧無以自給。

translations.literal: Gao was touring counties and saw an old woman white-haired and weeping; moved to pity he questioned her, and she replied, "I am a daughter-in-law of the Li family; I have two sons, Jun and E, who have been away in office for twenty years without returning; I am poor and have no means to support myself."
translations.idiomatic: While touring the counties Gao saw an elderly woman with white hair weeping by the roadside. Moved, he asked her story. She said, "I am a daughter-in-law of the Li family. I have two sons, Jun and E, who have held office away from home for twenty years without returning. I am too poor to support myself."

sentences.zh: 」時鈞為殿中侍御史，鍔為京兆府法曹，俱以文藝登科，名重於時。

translations.literal: At that time Jun was attendant censor within the palace and E was law officer in the Jingzhao prefectural office; both had passed the examinations by literary arts and were weighty in name in their time.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jun was a palace attendant censor and E was a legal officer in the Jingzhao metropolitan office. Both had passed the civil examinations on literary merit and enjoyed high reputations.

sentences.zh: 皋曰：「『入則孝，出則悌，行有餘力，然後可以學文。

translations.literal: Gao said, "'Entering then filial, going out then fraternal—when in conduct there is remaining strength, only then may one study the literary arts.'"
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "The Analects teach: 'At home be filial, abroad be respectful; only when you still have energy left may you study the classics.'"

sentences.zh: 』若二子者，豈可備於列位！

translations.literal: Men such as these two—how could they fill places in the ranks!"
translations.idiomatic: Men like these two are unfit to hold office!"

sentences.zh: 」由是舉奏，並除名勿齒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized in accusation and both were struck from the rolls and not counted among officials.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized against them, and both were struck from the rolls of officials.

sentences.zh: 改處州別駕，行州事，以良政聞。

translations.literal: He was changed to Chuzhou assistant prefect, administered prefectural affairs, and was known for good government.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to assistant prefect of Chuzhou, where he administered the prefecture and earned a reputation for good government.

sentences.zh: 征至京，未召見，因上書言理道，拜衡州刺史。

translations.literal: Summoned to the capital, before audience he memorialized on the principles of government and was appointed prefect of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the capital but not yet received in audience, he submitted a memorial on principles of government and was appointed prefect of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐小法，貶潮州刺史。

translations.literal: On a minor law he was demoted to prefect of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later demoted for a minor infraction to prefect of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 時楊炎謫官道州，知皋事直，及為相，復拜衡州。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Yan was demoted to office in Daozhou and knew Gao's affairs were upright; when he became chief minister, Gao was again appointed to Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan had been demoted to Daozhou and knew Gao to be upright. When Yang became chief minister, Gao was restored to Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，皋為御史覆訊，懼貽太妃憂，竟出則素服，入則公服，言貌如平常，太妃竟不知。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gao as censor conducted reinvestigation, he feared to bring grief to the consort dowager; when he went out he wore plain dress, when he entered official dress, words and appearance as in ordinary times—the consort dowager in the end did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gao served as a censor conducting reinvestigations, he feared distressing his mother. He wore plain dress when he went out and official robes when he entered her presence, speaking and behaving as usual, so that she never learned of his troubles.

sentences.zh: 及為潮州，詭詞謂遷，至是復位，方泣以白，且言非疾不敢有聞。

translations.literal: When he became Chaozhou prefect he used deceptive words saying it was a transfer; only when he was restored to position did he weep and inform her, and said that except for illness he dared not let her have news.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sent to Chaozhou he told her only that he was being transferred. Only when he was restored did he weep and tell her the truth, saying that except in cases of illness he had never dared let her hear bad news.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，遷湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong he was transferred to observation commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong he was appointed observation commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 前使辛京杲貪殘，有將王國良鎮邵州武岡縣，豪富，京杲以死罪加之。

translations.literal: The previous commissioner Xin Jinggao was greedy and cruel; there was a general Wang Guoliang garrisoning Wugang County in Shaozhou, wealthy and powerful; Jinggao imposed the death penalty on him.
translations.idiomatic: His predecessor Xin Jinggao was greedy and cruel. A general named Wang Guoliang, stationed at Wugang in Shaozhou, was wealthy and powerful. Jinggao condemned him to death.

sentences.zh: 國良危懼，因人所苦，遂散財聚眾據縣以叛，諸道同討，聯歲不能下。

translations.literal: Guoliang in peril and fear, because of what men suffered, thereupon scattered wealth and gathered a multitude, seized the county and rebelled; various circuits joined in suppression, and for successive years could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Wang Guoliang responded to the people's grievances by distributing his wealth, gathering followers, and seizing the county in rebellion. Troops from several circuits campaigned against him for years without success.

sentences.zh: 皋授命日，乃曰：「驅疲甿，誅反側，非所以奉聖朝事。

translations.literal: On the day Gao received his commission he said, "Driving weary commoners and executing those who turned aside is not the way to serve the holy dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: On the day he received his commission, Gao said, "Driving exhausted commoners and executing rebels is not how one serves the holy dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」遣使遺國良書曰；

translations.literal: " He sent an envoy to leave Guoliang a letter, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He sent an envoy with a letter to Wang Guoliang:

sentences.zh: 「觀將軍非敢大逆，蓋遭讒嫉，救誤死而已。

translations.literal: "I observe that the general does not dare great rebellion; he has merely suffered slander and envy and seeks to escape wrongful death.
translations.idiomatic: "I see that you never intended great treason. You were slandered and envied and sought only to escape an unjust death.

sentences.zh: 將軍遇我，何不速降？

translations.literal: The general meets me—why not surrender quickly?"
translations.idiomatic: Now that you face me, why not surrender at once?"

sentences.zh: 我與將軍同為辛京杲所構，我已蒙聖朝昭雪，使我何心持刃殺將軍耶！

translations.literal: The general and I were both framed by Xin Jinggao; I have already received exoneration from the holy court—what heart could make me hold a blade and kill the general!
translations.idiomatic: You and I were both framed by Xin Jinggao. The court has already cleared my name. How could I bear to draw a blade against you?

sentences.zh: 將軍以為不然，我以陣術破將軍陣，以攻法屠將軍城，非將軍所度也。

translations.literal: If the general thinks otherwise, I shall by battle array break the general's array and by assault methods slaughter the general's city—this is not what the general can measure."
translations.idiomatic: If you disagree, I will break your formations with mine and take your city by siege—more than you expect."

sentences.zh: 」國良捧書，且憂且喜，遣使請降，亦未必決。

translations.literal: Guoliang held the letter, both worried and pleased, sent an envoy to request surrender, yet was not necessarily resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang read the letter with mingled fear and hope and sent envoys to offer surrender, though he had not yet made a firm decision.

sentences.zh: 皋即日赴縣受降，中道有候騎馳告曰：「國良軍中有變，言降是詐也。

translations.literal: Gao that same day went to the county to accept surrender; on the way a scout galloped to report, "There is a change in Guoliang's army; the talk of surrender is a ruse."
translations.idiomatic: That same day Gao set out to accept the surrender in person. On the road a scout galloped up and said, "There is trouble in Guoliang's camp—the offer to surrender is a trick."

sentences.zh: 」皋曰：「非爾輩所知。

translations.literal: Gao said, "This is not for you to know."
translations.idiomatic: Gao said, "That is beyond your understanding."

sentences.zh: 」遂留麾下兵，單騎假稱使者，逕入國良壘中。

translations.literal: He thereupon left his troops behind, went alone on horseback pretending to be an envoy, and went straight into Guoliang's camp.
translations.idiomatic: He left his troops behind, rode alone into the camp disguised as an envoy, and went straight in.

sentences.zh: 國良召使者入，皋遂大叫軍中曰：「有人識曹王否？

translations.literal: Guoliang summoned the envoy in; Gao then shouted in the army, "Does anyone recognize the Prince of Cao?"
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang summoned the envoy inside. Gao then shouted through the camp, "Does anyone here know the Prince of Cao?"

sentences.zh: 只我是。

translations.literal: It is only I.
translations.idiomatic: I am he.

sentences.zh: 國良何不速降？

translations.literal: Guoliang, why not surrender quickly?"
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang, why do you not surrender at once?"

sentences.zh: 」一軍愕眙不敢動。

translations.literal: The whole army stared in shock and dared not move.
translations.idiomatic: The whole army stood stunned and motionless.

sentences.zh: 適有識者走至，傳呼曰：「是」。

translations.literal: Presently someone who recognized him ran up and passed the cry, "It is he."
translations.idiomatic: Then someone who knew him ran forward shouting, "It is he!"

sentences.zh: 國良匍匐叩頭請罪。

translations.literal: Guoliang crawled prostrate and knocked his head asking pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Guoliang prostrated himself and begged forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 皋執手約為兄弟，盡焚攻守之備，散倉庫，給兵士，令復農桑。

translations.literal: Gao took his hand and pledged brotherhood, burned all preparations for attack and defense, opened the storehouses, supplied the soldiers, and ordered a return to farming and sericulture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao took his hand and pledged brotherhood with him, burned all siege works and defenses, opened the granaries, paid the troops, and ordered the people back to farming.

sentences.zh: 有詔赦國良罪，賜名惟新。

translations.literal: An edict pardoned Guoliang's crime and granted the name Weixin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict pardoned Guoliang and granted him the name Weixin.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，丁母艱，奉喪至江陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianzhong he mourned his mother's death and escorted the coffin to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianzhong he entered mourning for his mother and escorted her coffin to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 會梁崇義反，乃授起復左衛大將軍，復還湖南，尋加散騎常侍李希烈反，遷江西道節度使、洪州刺史、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: It happened that Liang Chongyi rebelled; he was then given mourning leave as left guard general, returned again to Hunan, soon added as irregular attendant, and when Li Xilie rebelled was transferred to Jiangxi circuit military commissioner, Hongzhou prefect, and concurrently grand censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Chongyi rebelled, Gao was recalled from mourning as left guard general and sent back to Hunan. He was soon made irregular attendant. When Li Xilie rebelled, he was appointed military commissioner of Jiangxi, prefect of Hongzhou, and concurrently grand censor.

sentences.zh: 至州，集將吏而令曰：「嘗有功未申者，別為行；

translations.literal: On reaching the prefecture he gathered generals and clerks and ordered, "Those who have had merit not yet reported, form a separate line;
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his post he assembled his officers and said, "Those who have unreported achievements, step forward;

sentences.zh: 有策謀及器能堪佐軍者，別為行。

translations.literal: those with stratagems and capacity fit to assist the army, form a separate line."
translations.idiomatic: those with counsel or ability fit to assist the army, step forward as well."

sentences.zh: 」有裨將伊慎、李伯潛、劉旻皆自占，皋察其詞氣，驗其有功，悉補大將。

translations.literal: The subordinate generals Yi Shen, Li Boqian, and Liu Min all stepped forward of themselves; Gao observed their words and bearing, verified their achievements, and all were appointed great generals.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate generals Yi Shen, Li Boqian, and Liu Min all came forward. Gao judged their words and bearing, verified their records, and appointed them all senior generals.

sentences.zh: 擢王鍔委之中軍，以馬彝、許孟容為賓佐。

translations.literal: He promoted Wang E and entrusted him with the central army; he took Ma Yi and Xu Mengrong as guest aides.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted Wang E to command the central army and took Ma Yi and Xu Mengrong as his chief advisers.

sentences.zh: 繕甲兵，具戰艦，將軍二萬餘。

translations.literal: He repaired armor and weapons, equipped war vessels, and had more than twenty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired arms and armor, built warships, and mustered more than twenty thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 初，伊慎將江西兵從李希烈平襄州，及反，懼皋任之，乃陰遣遺之鎖甲，又詐為慎書往復，置遺於境。

translations.literal: Earlier Yi Shen had led Jiangxi troops following Li Xilie to pacify Xiangzhou; when Xilie rebelled, fearing Gao would employ him, Xilie secretly sent him chain armor as a gift and also forged letters back and forth in Shen's name, placing the gifts at the border.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yi Shen had led Jiangxi troops under Li Xilie to pacify Xiangzhou. When Xilie rebelled he feared Gao would use Shen against him, so he secretly sent Shen suits of mail and forged letters exchanged in Shen's name, leaving the gifts at the border.

sentences.zh: 上聞，即遣中使斬慎，皋表請捨令自效。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and at once sent a palace envoy to execute Shen; Gao memorialized asking to spare him and let him prove himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of this and sent a palace envoy to execute Shen. Gao memorialized asking that Shen be spared to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 會與賊夾江為陣，中使又至，皋乃勉令以功自贖，賜之以所乘馬及器甲，令將鋒而先，皋率軍繼之，責其有功，果大破賊，斬首數百級，慎方得免罪。

translations.literal: It happened that they faced the rebels across the river in battle array; the palace envoy came again; Gao then urged Shen to redeem himself by merit, gave him his own mount and armor, ordered him to lead the vanguard, Gao followed with the army and charged him to achieve merit; he indeed inflicted a great defeat on the rebels and beheaded several hundred; only then did Shen escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: As the armies faced each other across the river, another palace envoy arrived. Gao urged Shen to redeem himself by merit, gave him his own horse and armor, and ordered him to lead the vanguard while Gao followed with the main force. Shen won a crushing victory and took several hundred heads, and only then was he spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 賊樹堡柵於蔡山，皋度峻險不可攻，乃聲言西取蘄州，理戰艦，分兵傍南涯，與舟師溯江而上。

translations.literal: The rebels built fortifications and palisades at Cai Mountain; Gao judged the steep peril impassable to assault, so he proclaimed he would take Qizhou to the west, prepared war vessels, divided troops along the southern bank, and with the fleet went upriver.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fortified Cai Mountain. Gao judged the terrain too steep to assault directly, so he announced a move west against Qizhou, prepared his fleet, sent troops along the southern bank, and sailed upriver with his warships.

sentences.zh: 賊以老弱守柵，引軍循江隨戰艦，南北與皋兵相直。

translations.literal: The rebels left the old and weak to guard the palisades and led their army along the river following the war vessels, north and south facing Gao's troops directly.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels left the aged and weak to hold the palisades and marched along the river after the fleet, drawing up north and south to face Gao's troops.

sentences.zh: 去蔡山三百餘里，皋令步兵登舟，順流東下，不日拔蔡山。

translations.literal: More than three hundred li from Cai Mountain, Gao ordered the infantry to board the vessels and go downstream east; within days he took Cai Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When they were more than three hundred li from Cai Mountain, Gao had his infantry board the ships and sail downstream. Within days they seized Cai Mountain.

sentences.zh: 賊還救，間一日方至，大破之，因進拔蘄州，降其將李良，又取黃州，斬首千餘，兵益振，舒王為元帥，加皋前軍兵馬使。

translations.literal: The rebels returned to rescue; only after a day's interval did they arrive; he inflicted a great defeat, then advanced and took Qizhou, accepted the surrender of their general Li Liang, also took Huangzhou, beheaded more than a thousand; the army grew more vigorous; the Prince of Shu was supreme commander and added to Gao the post of forward-army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels turned back to relieve the position but arrived a day too late and were routed. Gao then advanced to take Qizhou, accepted the surrender of the rebel general Li Liang, and seized Huangzhou as well, taking more than a thousand heads. His army's morale soared. The Prince of Shu served as supreme commander and appointed Gao forward-army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 德宗居奉天，淮南節度陳少游強取鹽鐵錢，其使包佶以財幣溯江，次於蘄口。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong resided at Fengtian; Huainan military commissioner Chen Shaoyou forcibly seized salt and iron funds; his envoy Bao Ji with wealth and goods went up the river and halted at Qikou.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Dezong was at Fengtian, Huainan commissioner Chen Shaoyou forcibly seized salt and iron revenues. The envoy Bao Ji was transporting funds upriver and halted at Qikou.

sentences.zh: 時希烈已屠汴州，又遣驍將杜少誠將步騎萬餘來寇蘄、黃，將絕江道。

translations.literal: At that time Xilie had already slaughtered Bianzhou and again sent the fierce general Du Shaocheng leading more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Qi and Huang, intending to cut the river route.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie had already sacked Bianzhou and now sent the fierce general Du Shaocheng with more than ten thousand foot and horse to attack Qi and Huang, intending to cut the river route.

sentences.zh: 皋遣伊慎將七千眾御之，遇於永安戍。

translations.literal: Gao sent Yi Shen leading seven thousand to resist; they met at Yong'an garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent Yi Shen with seven thousand men to meet them at Yong'an garrison.

sentences.zh: 慎列三柵，相去才四里，列鼓角中柵。

translations.literal: Shen arrayed three palisades only four li apart and placed drums and horns in the central palisade.
translations.idiomatic: Shen set up three camps only four li apart, with drums and horns in the central camp.

sentences.zh: 少誠至，分兵圍之，部隊未嚴，聲鼓而三柵齊出奮擊，不為行陣，賊亂，少誠敗走，斬首萬級，封屍為京觀。

translations.literal: Shaocheng arrived and divided troops to surround them; the formations were not yet strict when drums sounded and all three palisades sallied together in fierce attack without formal battle lines; the rebels were in disorder, Shaocheng fled in defeat, ten thousand heads were cut, and the corpses were piled into a victory mound.
translations.idiomatic: Shaocheng arrived and divided his force to surround the camps. Before his lines were set, drums sounded and all three camps charged at once without keeping formation. The rebels broke. Shaocheng fled. Ten thousand heads were taken and the corpses were heaped into a victory mound.

sentences.zh: 以功加銀青光祿大夫，進封五百戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was given silver-blue gleam grand master and an added fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: For this merit he was made silver-blue gleam grand master of the palace and granted an additional fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 上至梁州，進獻繼至。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached Liangzhou, tributes of submission followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached Liangzhou, Gao's submissions of tribute arrived one after another.

sentences.zh: 皋以上蒙塵於外，不敢居城府，乃於西塞山上游大洲屯軍，從近縣為軍市，商貨畢至。

translations.literal: Because the emperor above was dust-stained abroad, Gao dared not dwell in the prefectural city; he therefore encamped his army on Dayu islet in the upper reaches of Xisai Mountain, made military markets from nearby counties, and merchants' goods all arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor was in exile, Gao would not occupy the prefectural seat. He encamped on Dayu islet in the upper Xisai Mountains, set up army markets in nearby counties, and merchants flocked there.

sentences.zh: 加工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was additionally made minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed minister of works.

sentences.zh: 駕還京師，又遣伊慎、王鍔將兵圍安州，州城阻□水為固，攻之累日不下。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he again sent Yi Shen and Wang E leading troops to besiege Anzhou; the prefectural city was fortified by blocking the river water and could not be taken for many days of assault.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Gao again sent Yi Shen and Wang E to besiege Anzhou. The city was fortified by the river and resisted for many days.

sentences.zh: 希烈遣甥劉戒虛將步八千來援。

translations.literal: Xilie sent his nephew Liu Jiexu leading eight thousand infantry as relief.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie sent his nephew Liu Jiexu with eight thousand foot soldiers as relief.

sentences.zh: 皋命李伯潛分師迎擊於應山，獲戒虛及大將二、裨將二十，斬首千餘。

translations.literal: Gao ordered Li Boqian to divide the army and meet the attack at Yingshan; he captured Jiexu and two great generals and twenty subordinate generals and beheaded more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Gao ordered Li Boqian to intercept them at Yingshan. He captured Jiexu, two senior generals, and twenty subordinate officers, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 面縛戒虛等之城下，乃使人說之，賊曰：「得大將及賓佐一二人為信，當降。

translations.literal: With faces bound he presented Jiexu and the others below the city wall, then sent men to persuade them; the rebels said, "If we obtain one or two great generals and guest aides as pledge, we will surrender."
translations.idiomatic: He bound the prisoners and displayed them below the walls, then sent envoys to negotiate. The defenders said, "Give us one or two senior officers or advisers as hostages and we will surrender."

sentences.zh: 」皋乃使王鍔、馬彝繩城而入，城中大呼，乃出降。

translations.literal: Gao then had Wang E and Ma Yi rope their way into the city; the city shouted loudly and thereupon came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sent Wang E and Ma Yi up the walls on ropes. The city erupted in shouts and then surrendered.

sentences.zh: 希烈又遣兵援隨州，皋令伊慎擊於厲鄉，大破之，復平靜、白雁等關。

translations.literal: Xilie again sent troops to relieve Suizhou; Gao ordered Yi Shen to strike at Lixiang, inflicted a great defeat, and again pacified Jing, Baiyan, and other passes.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie sent another force to relieve Suizhou. Gao ordered Yi Shen to attack at Lixiang, won a great victory, and recovered the passes of Jing, Baiyan, and others.

sentences.zh: 希烈懼，乃戢兵。

translations.literal: Xilie was afraid and thereupon restrained his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xilie was frightened and restrained his troops.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，拜江陵尹、荊南節度等使，江漢倚皋為固。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was appointed Jiangling metropolitan governor and Jingnan military commissioner and the like; the Jiang and Han regions relied on Gao as their stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhenyuan he was appointed metropolitan governor of Jiangling and military commissioner of Jingnan. The middle Yangzi relied on him as its bulwark.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李思登以隨州降。

translations.literal: Before long Li Sideng surrendered Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Sideng surrendered Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 凡下州四、縣十七，大小十餘陣，未嘗敗衄。

translations.literal: In all he reduced four prefectures and seventeen counties, in large and small more than ten battles, and never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In all he captured four prefectures and seventeen counties in more than ten engagements, large and small, without ever suffering defeat.

sentences.zh: 淮西既平，請護喪祔東都，上遣中使吊，贈父右僕射，母曹國太妃。

translations.literal: When Huai West was pacified, he requested to escort the coffin for enshrinement in the eastern capital; the emperor sent a palace envoy to condole, enfeoffed his father as right vice director, and his mother as consort of Cao.
translations.idiomatic: After Huai West was pacified he asked to escort his father's remains for burial in the eastern capital. The emperor sent a palace envoy to offer condolences, posthumously enfeoffed his father as right vice director, and his mother as princess of Cao.

sentences.zh: 葬畢來朝，詔還鎮，出東都以拜墓，觀者榮之。

translations.literal: When the burial was complete he came to court; an edict ordered him back to his command; passing out of the eastern capital to visit the tomb, onlookers counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he came to court and was ordered back to his command. When he left the eastern capital to visit the tomb, onlookers regarded it as a mark of honor.

sentences.zh: 先，江陵東北有廢田傍漢古堤二處，每夏則溢，皋始命塞之，廣田五千頃，畝得一鐘。

translations.literal: Earlier northeast of Jiangling there were abandoned fields beside two ancient Han embankments; every summer they overflowed; Gao first ordered them blocked, extending fields five thousand qing, each mu yielding one zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, northeast of Jiangling lay abandoned fields beside two ancient Han dikes that flooded every summer. Gao ordered them repaired and reclaimed five thousand qing of land, each mu yielding a full zhong of grain.

sentences.zh: 規江南廢洲為廬捨，架江為二橋，流人自占二千餘戶。

translations.literal: He planned abandoned islets south of the river as dwellings, spanned the river with two bridges, and displaced persons of themselves occupied more than two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out abandoned river islets for housing, built two bridges across the river, and more than two thousand refugee households settled there on their own.

sentences.zh: 自荊至樂鄉凡二百里，旅舍鄉聚凡十數，大者皆數百家。

translations.literal: From Jing to Lexiang altogether two hundred li, inns and village clusters numbered more than ten, the large ones all several hundred families.
translations.idiomatic: From Jing to Lexiang, two hundred li along the route, he established more than ten inns and market towns, the largest with several hundred households each.

sentences.zh: 楚俗佻薄，不穿井，飲陂澤，皋始命合錢開井以便人。

translations.literal: Chu custom was frivolous and shallow; they did not dig wells and drank from ponds and marshes; Gao first ordered pooled funds to open wells for people's convenience.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chu were careless in custom, drank from ponds rather than wells, and Gao first ordered public funds pooled to dig wells for their convenience.

sentences.zh: 初平希烈，吳少誠殺陳仙奇，上以襄、鄧要厄，三年，除襄州刺史、山南東道節度等使，割汝、隨隸焉。

translations.literal: When Xilie was first pacified, Wu Shaoqing killed Chen Xianqi; the emperor because Xiang and Deng were strategic passes, in the third year appointed him Xiangzhou prefect and Shannan East circuit military commissioner and the like, severing Ru and Sui to be subordinate.
translations.idiomatic: After Xilie was first pacified, Wu Shaoqing killed Chen Xianqi. Because Xiangyang and Dengzhou were strategic passes, in the third year Gao was appointed prefect of Xiangzhou and military commissioner of Shannan East, with Ru and Sui placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 練兵積糧，市回鶻馬益騎兵，堂大畋以教士，少誠憚之。

translations.literal: He trained troops and stored grain, bought Uighur horses to increase cavalry, held great hunts in the hall to instruct soldiers, and Shaoqing feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled troops, stockpiled grain, bought Uighur horses to strengthen his cavalry, and held great hunts to train his men. Shaoqing feared him.

sentences.zh: 性勤儉，知人疾苦，設監司，能參聽下，持將吏短長，賞罰必信。

translations.literal: By nature diligent and frugal, he knew men's hardships, established supervisory offices, could join in listening below, grasped generals' and clerks' strengths and weaknesses, and rewards and punishments were sure.
translations.idiomatic: He was diligent and frugal by nature, understood the people's hardships, set up supervisory offices, listened to reports from below, knew the strengths and weaknesses of his officers, and his rewards and punishments were always reliable.

sentences.zh: 所至常平物價，貴則出賣之，給將吏廩俸，豪家不得擅其利。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he stabilized market prices; when dear he sold out stores, supplied generals' and clerks' grain stipends, and powerful families could not monopolize the profit.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he stabilized prices, sold government stores when prices rose high, paid his officers' grain stipends from the proceeds, and kept powerful families from monopolizing profits.

sentences.zh: 常運心巧思為戰艦，挾二輪蹈之，翔風鼓浪，疾若掛帆席，所造省易而久固。

translations.literal: He often applied ingenious thought to war vessels, with two wheels tread upon them; soaring wind stirred waves, swift as hanging sail cloth; what he made was economical and easy yet long-lasting and firm.
translations.idiomatic: He often applied his ingenuity to warships fitted with tread wheels that caught the wind and drove through the waves as swiftly as sails, yet were simple to build and durable.

sentences.zh: 又造欹器，進入內中。

translations.literal: He also made tipping vessels and presented them within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also made tipping vessels and presented them to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 每遺人物，常自秤量。

translations.literal: Whenever he sent gifts he always weighed them himself.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sent gifts he weighed them himself.

sentences.zh: 署之官匹帛皆印之，絕吏之私。

translations.literal: Official bolts of silk he marked all with seals, cutting off clerks' private gain.
translations.idiomatic: He stamped every official bolt of silk distributed, cutting off clerks' private gain.

sentences.zh: 初，扶風馬彝未知名，皋始辟之，卒以正直稱。

translations.literal: Earlier Fufeng Ma Yi was not yet known by name; Gao first recruited him and in the end he was known for uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ma Yi of Fufeng was unknown when Gao first recruited him, and he ended his career with a reputation for integrity.

sentences.zh: 漢陽王張柬之有林園在州西，公府多假之游宴，皋將買之，彝斂衽而言曰：「張漢陽有中興功，今遺業當百代保之，王縱欲之，奈何令其子孫自鬻焉！

translations.literal: Prince of Hanyang Zhang Jianzhi had a grove garden west of the prefecture; government offices often borrowed it for excursions and feasts; Gao was about to buy it; Ma Yi straightened his robe and said, "Zhang of Hanyang has merit in restoring the dynasty; his remaining estate should be preserved for a hundred generations—though Your Highness may desire it, how could you have his descendants sell it themselves!"
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hanyang Zhang Jianzhi had an estate west of the city that officials often borrowed for outings. When Gao was about to buy it, Ma Yi straightened his robes and said, "Zhang of Hanyang helped restore the dynasty. His estate should be preserved for generations. Even if Your Highness desires it, how can you have his descendants sell their patrimony?"

sentences.zh: 」皋謝曰：「主吏失詞，為足下羞；

translations.literal: Gao apologized, saying, "The chief clerk misspoke and has shamed you;
translations.idiomatic: Gao apologized and said, "My staff spoke wrongly and shamed you;

sentences.zh: 微足下，安得聞此言！

translations.literal: but for you, how could I have heard these words!"
translations.idiomatic: without you I would never have heard such words!"

sentences.zh: 」以改過遷善、知人任下為己任，故賓從將佐多至大官。

translations.literal: He took correcting faults and moving toward goodness and knowing men and employing subordinates as his charge; therefore guests, followers, generals, and aides mostly reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: He made correcting his faults, recognizing talent, and trusting subordinates his personal charge, and many of his advisers and officers rose to high office.

sentences.zh: 貞元八年三月，暴卒於位，年六十，廢朝三日，贈右僕射，賻吊有差，謚曰成。

translations.literal: In the third month of the eighth year of Zhenyuan he suddenly died in office, age sixty; court was suspended three days; he was posthumously given right vice director, funeral gifts and condolences in graded measure, posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the eighth year of Zhenyuan he died suddenly in office at the age of sixty. Court was suspended for three days. He was posthumously made right vice director, granted funeral gifts in due measure, and given the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 子象古、道古、復古。

translations.literal: His sons were Xianggu, Daogu, and Fugu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Xianggu, Daogu, and Fugu.

sentences.zh: 象古自衡州刺史為安南都護。

translations.literal: Xianggu from Hengzhou prefect became protector-general of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: Xianggu rose from prefect of Hengzhou to protector-general of Annan.

sentences.zh: 元和十四年，為楊清所殺，妻子支黨無焦類焉。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yuanhe he was killed by Yang Qing; wife, children, branch kin—none left whole.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yuanhe he was killed by Yang Qing. His wife, children, and kin were wiped out to the last.

sentences.zh: 楊清者，代為南方酋豪，屬象古貪縱，人心不附，又惡清之強，自驩州刺史召為牙門將，郁郁不快。

translations.literal: Yang Qing for generations was a southern chieftain; because Xianggu was greedy and unrestrained men's hearts did not attach; he also hated Qing's strength and summoned him from Huanzhou prefect to gate guard general; depressed and displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qing's family had long been southern chieftains. Xianggu was greedy and unrestrained, and the people did not support him. He also resented Qing's power, summoned him from the prefecture of Huan to serve as gate guard general, and Qing was deeply discontented.

sentences.zh: 無何，邕管黃家賊叛，詔象古發兵數道共討之，像古命清領兵三千赴焉。

translations.literal: Before long the Huang bandits of Yong and Guan rebelled; an edict ordered Xianggu to send troops on several routes jointly to suppress; Xianggu ordered Qing to lead three thousand troops thither.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Huang bandits of Yong and Guan rebelled. An edict ordered Xianggu to attack on several fronts. Xianggu sent Qing with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 清與其子志烈及所親杜士交潛謀回戈，夜襲安南，數日城陷，像古故及於害。

translations.literal: Qing with his son Zhilie and his intimate Du Shijiao secretly plotted to turn their blades, by night assaulted Annan, within days the city fell, and Xianggu therefore met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Qing, his son Zhilie, and his confidant Du Shijiao secretly plotted to turn their troops about. They attacked Annan by night, and within days the city fell. Xianggu was killed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷命唐州刺史桂仲武為都護，且招諭之。

translations.literal: The court appointed Tangzhou prefect Gui Zhongwu as protector-general and also summoned and instructed them.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Gui Zhongwu, prefect of Tangzhou, as protector-general and ordered him to offer terms of surrender.

sentences.zh: 赦清，以為瓊州刺史。

translations.literal: Qing was pardoned and made Qiongzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was pardoned and appointed prefect of Qiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 仲武至境，清不納，復約束部署，刑戮憯虐，人無聊生。

translations.literal: When Zhongwu reached the border, Qing would not receive him; again he imposed discipline and deployment, punishments cruel and savage, and men had no means to live.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongwu reached the border Qing refused to admit him, tightened his control, and punished with savage cruelty until the people could barely survive.

sentences.zh: 仲武使人諭其酋豪，數月間，歸附繼至，約兵七千餘人，收其城，斬清及其子志貞，籍沒其家。

translations.literal: Zhongwu sent men to instruct his chieftains; within several months submissions followed in succession; he mustered about seven thousand troops, recovered the city, beheaded Qing and his son Zhizhen, and confiscated their household.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu sent envoys to win over the local chieftains. Within months they submitted one after another. He gathered about seven thousand troops, retook the city, executed Qing and his son Zhizhen, and confiscated their property.

sentences.zh: 志烈與士交敗，保於長州之鑿溪，尋以所部兵來降。

translations.literal: Zhilie and Shijiao were defeated, held out at Zaoxi in Changzhou, and soon with the troops under their command came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhilie and Shijiao were defeated and held out at Zaoxi in Changzhou, but soon surrendered with the troops still under their command.

sentences.zh: 道古登進士第，遷司門員外郎。

translations.literal: Daogu passed the presented scholar examination and was transferred to vice director in the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Daogu passed the presented scholar examination and was appointed vice director in the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 便佞巧宦，早升朝籍，常以酒餚棋博游公卿門，角賭之際，每偽為不勝而厚償之，故當時有虛名，而嗜利者悉與之狎。

translations.literal: Fawning and clever in office, he early rose into court registers; he often with wine, food, chess, and gambling visited the doors of dukes and ministers; in contests of wagering he always pretended not to win and richly compensated them; therefore he had a hollow reputation in his time, and those who craved profit all were intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Smooth and clever in court politics, he rose early in the official ranks. He frequented the houses of high ministers with wine, food, chess, and gambling, and in wagers always pretended to lose and paid generously. He enjoyed a hollow reputation, and the profit-minded all courted him.

sentences.zh: 歷處、隨、唐、睦四州刺史，由黔中觀察為鄂、岳、沔、蘄、安、黃團練觀察使，時元和十一年也。

translations.literal: He successively served as prefect of Chu, Sui, Tang, and Mu; from Qianzhong observation commissioner he became training-and-militia observation commissioner of E, Yue, Mian, Qi, An, and Huang—it was the eleventh year of Yuanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as prefect of Chu, Sui, Tang, and Mu, then rose from observation commissioner of Qianzhong to training-and-militia observation commissioner of E, Yue, Mian, Qi, An, and Huang in the eleventh year of Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 初，以柳公綽在鎮無功，議將代之，裴度言：「道古嗣曹王皋之子，皋嘗以江漢兵遏希烈之亂，威惠至今在人，復用其子必能繼美。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Liu Gongchuo in the command had no achievement, it was discussed to replace him; Pei Du said, "Daogu succeeds the son of Prince of Cao Gao; Gao once with Jiang-Han troops checked Xilie's disorder, authority and kindness to this day remain in men—to again employ his son will surely be able to continue the excellence."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, because Liu Gongchuo had achieved nothing in command, the court discussed replacing him. Pei Du said, "Daogu is heir to Prince of Cao Li Gao, who once used the armies of the middle Yangzi to check Li Xilie's rebellion. His authority and kindness are still remembered. His son will surely continue that legacy."

sentences.zh: 」憲宗然之，故有此授。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong approved this, and therefore there was this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong agreed, and Daogu received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 及赴鎮，倍道而行，以數騎徑入安州城。

translations.literal: When he went to his command he traveled double marches, and with several horsemen went straight into Anzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to take up command he traveled at double speed and entered Anzhou with only a few horsemen.

sentences.zh: 時公綽殊未意道古至，惶駭而出，家財多為所奪。

translations.literal: At that time Gongchuo had not at all expected Daogu to arrive; in panic and alarm he went out, and much of his household wealth was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Gongchuo had not expected Daogu so soon. He fled in alarm, and much of his household property was seized.

sentences.zh: 十二年，道古攻申州，克其羅城，乃進圍逼其中城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Daogu attacked Shenzhou, took its outer wall, then advanced to besiege and press the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Daogu attacked Shenzhou, took the outer wall, and advanced to besiege the inner city.

sentences.zh: 城中守卒夜帥婦人登城而呼，懸門竊發，分出其眾，道古之眾驚亂，為虜所殺。

translations.literal: The garrison defenders by night led women atop the wall to shout; they lowered the gate in secret and sallied, dividing out their multitude; Daogu's troops were alarmed and in disorder and were killed by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders by night led women onto the walls to shout, secretly opened the gates, and sallied out in force. Daogu's troops panicked and were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 初，李聽守安州，未嘗退衄。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Ting garrisoned Anzhou and had never suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Ting had held Anzhou and never suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 及道古至，誣奏聽，移去之，乃自帥兵出穆陵。

translations.literal: When Daogu arrived he memorialized falsely against Ting, had him removed, and then himself led troops out through Muleng.
translations.idiomatic: When Daogu arrived he falsely memorialized against Li Ting, had him removed, and led the army out through Muleng himself.

sentences.zh: 士卒驕惰，賜給多闕，其度支供軍錢，道古半以奉權倖，半以沒己，人皆怨怒，不肯力戰。

translations.literal: The soldiers were arrogant and lazy, grants and supplies much lacking; the funds the revenue bureau supplied for the army—half Daogu used to serve the powerful and favored, half to enrich himself; all men were resentful and angry and would not fight with full strength.
translations.idiomatic: His troops grew arrogant and slack, and rations were often short. Half the army funds from the revenue bureau he gave to favorites at court and half he kept for himself. The men were furious and refused to fight wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 賊亦易道古，以羸兵抵之，故道古前後再攻破申州外城而不能拔。

translations.literal: The rebels also despised Daogu and met him with weak troops; therefore Daogu before and after twice broke Shenzhou's outer wall yet could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels also despised Daogu and met him with inferior troops. He twice breached the outer wall of Shenzhou but could never take the city.

sentences.zh: 至李愬入蔡州，乃降。

translations.literal: When Li Su entered Caizhou, they then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Li Su entered Caizhou did they surrender.

sentences.zh: 元和十三年，入為宗正卿。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he entered the capital as director of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yuanhe he entered the capital as director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 道古在鄂州日，以貪暴聞，懼終得罪，乃薦山人柳泌以媚於上。

translations.literal: In Daogu's days at Ezhou he was known for greed and violence; fearing he would in the end offend and be punished, he recommended the mountain man Liu Bi to flatter the emperor above.
translations.idiomatic: While at Ezhou Daogu was known for greed and cruelty. Fearing eventual punishment, he recommended the mountaineer Liu Bi to curry favor with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 後又為左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later he again served as general of the Left Gold Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as general of the Left Gold Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 憲宗季年頗信方士，銳於服食，詔天下搜訪奇士。

translations.literal: In his late years Emperor Xianzong greatly trusted alchemical masters and was keen on ingesting elixirs; he edicted the empire to search out extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Emperor Xianzong greatly trusted Daoist alchemists and was eager to take elixirs. He ordered a search throughout the empire for extraordinary men.

sentences.zh: 宰相皇甫鎛方諛媚固寵，道古言柳泌有道術，鎛得進之，待詔翰林。

translations.literal: Chief minister Huangfu Bo was then flattering to secure favor; Daogu said Liu Bi had Daoist arts; Bo was able to advance him, and he awaited edicts in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Huangfu Bo was then currying favor through flattery. Daogu claimed that Liu Bi possessed Daoist arts. Bo had him presented to the throne, and Liu Bi awaited imperial orders in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 憲宗服餌過當，暴成狂躁之疾，以至棄代。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong ingested elixirs in excess and suddenly developed a violent, frenzied illness, until he abandoned the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong took the elixirs in excess and suddenly fell into a violent frenzy of illness, until at last he died.

sentences.zh: 穆宗在東宮，扼腕於其事，及居喪，皆竄逐誅之。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong in the eastern palace wrung his wrists at this affair; when he held mourning, all were driven out in exile and executed.
translations.idiomatic: While still heir apparent, Emperor Muzong was deeply grieved by these events. Once he succeeded and entered mourning, he had all those involved driven out and executed.

sentences.zh: 鎛既貶責，授道古循州司馬，終以服丹藥，歐血而卒。

translations.literal: When Bo was already demoted and punished, Daogu was appointed Xunzhou staff officer; in the end because he took elixir medicines he vomited blood and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Bo was demoted and punished, Daogu was appointed staff officer of Xunzhou. He eventually died vomiting blood from the elixirs he had taken.

sentences.zh: 【史贊】

translations.literal: Historian's Commendation
translations.idiomatic: Historian's Commendation

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：李勉、李皋，稟性端莊，處身廉潔，臨民蒞事，動有美聲，可謂宗臣之英也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Li Mian and Li Gao received nature upright and grave, conducted themselves incorrupt, in facing the people and attending to affairs their every move had fine repute—they may be called the flower of imperial clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Li Mian and Li Gao were upright and grave by nature, incorruptible in conduct, and wherever they governed the people their administration won praise. They may truly be called exemplars of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 若夫治軍旅，禦寇戎，謀必臧，戰必勝，則又勉不及皋遠矣。

translations.literal: As for governing armies, resisting border foes, plans always good and battles always victorious—here again Mian fell far short of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: But in training armies, repelling invaders, planning with unfailing soundness, and fighting with unfailing victory, Mian fell far short of Gao.

sentences.zh: 道古便佞，奸以事君，何父子之不相類也。

translations.literal: Daogu was fawning and wicked in serving his lord—how father and son were not alike!
translations.idiomatic: Daogu was smooth and treacherous in serving his sovereign. How unlike father and son they were!

sentences.zh: 贊曰：我宗之英，曰皋與勉，才雖不同，道豈相遠。

translations.literal: The commendation says: The flower of our clan are called Gao and Mian; talent though not the same, in the Way how could they be far apart.
translations.idiomatic: Commendation: The flower of our clan are Gao and Mian. Their talents differed, yet in moral conduct how far apart could they be?
